title: Start New Year by Setting Reasonable Learning Goals
titleZh: 通过设定合理的学习目标来开启新年
credits: John Russell wrote this lesson for Learning English. George Grow was the editor.

sentences.en: For VOA Learning English, this is the Education Report.
sentences.zh: 对于美国之音英语学习，这是教育报道。

sentences.en: Learning a new language is a long, difficult process.
sentences.zh: 学习一门新语言是一个漫长而艰难的过程。

sentences.en: This process can become easier if you set goals.
sentences.zh: 如果你设定目标，这个过程可能会变得更容易。

sentences.en: Goals help guide language learners and give them reasons to continue studying a language.
sentences.zh: 目标能够指导语言学习者，并为他们提供继续学习语言的理由。

sentences.en: However, if you set unreasonable goals, then you will probably become discouraged.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你设定了不切实际的目标，那么你可能很可能会变得气馁。

sentences.en: Many English learners set difficult, even unreasonable goals.
sentences.zh: 许多英语学习者设定了困难甚至不切实际的目标。

sentences.en: For example, here at VOA Learning English, we often read emails with comments like: "My goal is to sound like a native speaker..." or "My goal is to lose my accent."
sentences.zh: 例如，在这里的美国之音英语学习，我们经常读到这样的邮件，评论说：“我的目标是说得像母语者一样……”或“我的目标是消除我的口音。”

sentences.en: The problem with the goal of sounding like a native speaker is that it is not a reasonable goal for many people.
sentences.zh: 以说得像母语者为目标的问题在于，对许多人来说这不是一个合理的目标。

sentences.en: When English learners begin studying English after a certain age, they are not able to sound exactly like a native English speaker.
sentences.zh: 当英语学习者在某个年龄之后开始学习英语时，他们无法说得像母语英语者那样。

sentences.en: That is the opinion of Eli Hinkel, a professor at Seattle Pacific University.
sentences.zh: 这是西雅图太平洋大学教授埃利·欣克尔的观点。

sentences.en: She says that people who have not reached puberty still have enough muscle and brain plasticity to allow their brain to control their mouth muscles.
sentences.zh: 她说，尚未进入青春期的孩子仍有足够的肌肉和大脑可塑性，让大脑能够控制他们的嘴部肌肉。

sentences.en: Puberty is the period of life when a child becomes an adult.
sentences.zh: 青春期是孩子成长为成年人的阶段。

sentences.en: After your physical growth has stopped, the brain loses some of its ability to change the way it controls the muscles of the mouth.
sentences.zh: 当你的身体发育停止后，大脑会失去一部分改变其控制嘴部肌肉方式的能力。

sentences.en: This is what results in an accent, according to Hinkel.
sentences.zh: 据欣克尔所说，这就是口音产生的原因。

sentences.en: In other words, having an accent is a natural part of the aging process of the brain.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，拥有口音是大脑老化过程中的自然部分。

sentences.en: Just because you might not sound like a native speaker does not mean that you should give up trying to improve your pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为你可能说得不像母语者，并不意味着你应该放弃努力提高你的发音。

sentences.en: And just because you have an accent does not mean that your language skills are poor.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为你有口音，并不意味着你的语言技能很差。

sentences.en: Hinkel suggested that English learners should not be too disheartened about their accents.
sentences.zh: 欣克尔建议英语学习者不要对他们的口音过于灰心丧气。

sentences.en: "So, there is really no connection between the quality of one's language and the accent."
sentences.zh: “所以，一个人的语言质量与口音之间真的没有联系。”

sentences.en: She adds that there are even benefits to having an accent.
sentences.zh: 她还补充说，拥有口音甚至有一些好处。

sentences.en: Eli Hinkel is a native Russian speaker.
sentences.zh: E利·欣克尔是俄语母语者。

sentences.en: But she works as a professor in a Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL) program.
sentences.zh: 但她在英语作为第二语言教学（TESL）项目里担任教授。

sentences.en: She believes her accent helps her when she is teaching students.
sentences.zh: 她相信自己的口音在教学生时能帮上忙。

sentences.en: "I teach MA TESL courses …So, my students think that I really, really know what I'm talking about…accent goes a great deal toward that."
sentences.zh: “我教英语作为第二语言的硕士课程……所以，我的学生觉得我确实、确实懂得我所讲的内容……口音在这方面帮了大忙。”

sentences.en: Another teacher says sounding like a native speaker is not necessary.
sentences.zh: 另一位教师则认为，听起来像母语者并非必要。

sentences.en: Marla Yoshida is a Teaching English as a Foreign Language Teacher at the University of California, Irvine.
sentences.zh: 由良·吉田是加州大学欧文分校的英语作为外语教师。

sentences.en: She says that improving your pronunciation is definitely possible – if you choose a reasonable goal.
sentences.zh: 她说，改善发音是完全可能的——只要你设定一个合理的目标。

sentences.en: "You can reach a stage where your pronunciation is easy for people to understand, where it never causes a problem... you go into Starbucks and say your name, and they understand … you give your order and they understand.
sentences.zh: “你可以达到这样一个阶段：你的发音让别人听得懂，从不造成问题……你走进星巴克报出自己的名字，他们能听懂……你下单点单，他们也能听懂。

sentences.en: So, that's a reasonable goal: being understood easily.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个合理的目标：被轻松地理解。

sentences.en: Where sounding like a native speaker is wonderful if you can do it… it's not necessary."
sentences.zh: 如果能做到听起来像母语者当然很好……但并非必要。”

sentences.en: So, what can English learners do to improve their pronunciation?
sentences.zh: 那么，英语学习者能做些什么来改善发音呢？

sentences.en: Marla Yoshida says that, like when you decide to diet, you are more likely to have success if you set reasonable goals.
sentences.zh: 由良·吉田说，就像你决定节食一样，如果你设定合理的目标，就更有可能成功。

sentences.en: She suggests working on specific areas of pronunciation that you can improve, instead of trying to sound like a native speaker.
sentences.zh: 她建议针对你能改善的发音特定部分下功夫，而不是试图听起来像母语者。

sentences.en: "Work consciously, if you are an adult, to change the way you pronounce.
sentences.zh: “作为成年人，要有意识地改变你的发音方式。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a diet.
sentences.zh: 这有点像节食。

sentences.en: If you set a more reasonable goal... then, the diet might succeed.
sentences.zh: 如果你设定一个更合理的目标……那么，节食或许就能成功。

sentences.en: In the same way, pronunciation … if you have a more reasonable goal, like… 'I have trouble with the r and l sounds, so first I'm going try those.
sentences.zh: 同样地，发音……如果你有更合理的目标，比如……‘我在r和l这两个音上有困难，所以首先我要试着练好它们。

sentences.en: And then, when I'm comfortable with those, then I'll move on to some other sound that causes problems.' It takes time, but it is possible."
sentences.zh: 然后，当我对这两个音感到得心应手时，我再转到其他会造成问题的音上去。’这需要时间，但确实可行。”

sentences.en: Yoshida added that English learners should understand that improving their pronunciation can take a long time.
sentences.zh: 吉田补充说，英语学习者应当明白，改善发音可能需要很长时间。

sentences.en: She said that learners should not be tricked by people who claim to be able to help people get rid of their accents:
sentences.zh: 她说，学习者不应被那些声称能帮人去掉口音的人所蒙骗：

sentences.en: "It is good to realize that it [improving pronunciation] is not a fast process.
sentences.zh: 认识到这一点是件好事：[改善发音]并不是一个快速的过程。

sentences.en: Everyone has been speaking their native language for years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 每个人都已经说了好几年的母语了。

sentences.en: And it's hard to change.
sentences.zh: 而改变是很难的。

sentences.en: Habits of how you move your mouth are really hard to change.
sentences.zh: 你移动嘴巴的习惯真的很难改变。

sentences.en: So, don't expect miracles.
sentences.zh: 所以，不要指望出现奇迹。

sentences.en: Sometimes, people see advertisements for software or courses that say 'get rid of your accent in only five lessons'—or something...
sentences.zh: 有时，人们会看到一些软件或课程的广告，声称“只需五节课就能摆脱口音”——之类的说法……

sentences.en: It's not going to happen!
sentences.zh: 这是不可能实现的！

sentences.en: There are no miracles."
sentences.zh: 世上没有奇迹。”

sentences.en: So, what can you do?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: Start by setting a reasonable goal.
sentences.zh: 从设定一个合理的目标开始。

sentences.en: Choose one or two sounds that are difficult for you to pronounce.
sentences.zh: 选择一两个对你来说难以发音的音。

sentences.en: Then, work to improve those sounds.
sentences.zh: 然后，努力改善这些音。

sentences.en: When you have improved, study other sounds.
sentences.zh: 当你有所改进后，再学习其他音。

sentences.en: Progress might be slow for you, but don't give up!
sentences.zh: 对你来说，进步可能很慢，但请不要放弃！

sentences.en: Next week, we will give you examples of exercises that you can do to start improving your pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 下周，我们会给你一些练习的示例，你可以借此开始改善发音。

sentences.en: I'm John Russell.
sentences.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

glossary.def: a way of pronouncing words that occurs among the people in a particular region or country
the period of life when a person's sexual organs mature and he or she becomes able to have children
the quality of being able to be made into different shapes
the way in which a word or name is pronounced
